name: Knotlog
description: Persistent session memory for coding agents, kept as plain Markdown notes in a local folder (the vault). Search the vault, read its byte-budgeted session context, and append one line to today's session note. Nothing leaves the machine. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: knotlog_search and knotlog_context only read the vault. Both are capped at the vault's ctx_max byte budget (4096 by default), so one call cannot return more than the session start does.
knotlog_note is the only tool that writes: one line appended to today's session note, never a rewrite. It stays on review because notes can be found again in later sessions.
Notes matching a secret pattern (AWS, GitHub, Slack, Google keys, private keys) are refused before anything is written.
Set write_approval=on in .knotlog/config to queue notes for review with knotlog pending instead of writing them.
The server finds the vault from its working directory or KNOTLOG_VAULT. Register it from inside the vault you mean, so it reads that vault and no other.
